thread:
alerts-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary group 'canary-v3' is showing p99 latency > 6s on /generate (streaming stalls). Traffic share: 10%.
Emily SRE: paging @Darron Oncall — can you take this? p99 at 8.6s, p95 ~1.2s. Looks like tail only. :eyes:
Darron Oncall: on it. Joining call in 2m. linked metrics: https://grafana.redwood/d/abc123/canary-latency?orgId=1&view=p99
Priya ML: I see elevated KV cache miss rate for v3 in the runtime metrics, also a bump in memory churn on nodes running model:v3.1. Could be cache eviction thrashing with longer seqs.
Darron Oncall: seeing a cluster of streaming stall errors in the logs around 1820001185..1820001220. Attaching tail: ```
[streamer] WARN stall_detected id=xyz seq=4096 elapsed_ms=3200
[kvcache] INFO miss model=v3.1 shard=5 size=1.2GB
[runtime] ERROR slow_step model=v3.1 step=attention_kv
```
Emily SRE: estimate impact? any customer-facing errors?
Jules Support: Zendesk shows 3 high-priority tickets referencing slow responses from /chat-stream in the last 10m. Customers affected appear to be on dedicated + hosted. I'll flag them and notify CSMs.
Marc PM: how much traffic is on the canary? if it's 10% and p99 is 8.6s that's definitely user-visible. Thoughts on immediate mitigation?
Priya ML: quick mitigation options: 1) reduce canary traffic to 0% (stop rollout), 2) rollback to model:v3.0, 3) patch runtime to avoid eviction (slow). Option 1 or 2 are fastest.
Darron Oncall: agree. I'm going to shift canary routing to previous stable variant and scale down canary pods. Doing traffic-shift now. Command: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood/api/routing/shift" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/generate","from":"canary-v3","to":"stable-v3","percent":100}'
```
deploy-bot: Received routing change request. Applying: set route /generate: canary-v3 -> stable-v3 (100%).
deploy-bot: Routing change applied. Propagation started across edge nodes (delta window ~30s).
Darron Oncall: scaled canary pool down by 80% to drain in-flight requests. Issuing scale command: ```kubectl scale deployment canary-v3 --replicas=1 -n inference```
Priya ML: monitoring KV evictions and streamer stalls closely. If stalls persist after shift, we rollback model package entirely.
Emily SRE: initial post-shift metrics — p99 dropped from 8.6s -> 1.1s within 45s of change. p95 steady at ~1.1s.
alerts-bot: :white_check_mark: p99 threshold cleared on /generate. Current p99=1.05s, p95=1.08s. No new streaming stalls in last 2m.
Jules Support: Notifying the three impacted customers: we estimate ~12% of their requests experienced latency >5s. Sending courtesy messages and incident acknowledgement now.
Marc PM: we'll open a follow-up incident for cause analysis and RCA. Action items: Priya to analyze KV cache behavior, Emily to collect runtime traces, Darron to produce exact traffic shift timeline.
Darron Oncall: Creating incident ticket: https://internal.redwood/incidents/IR-2026-045 (assigned SRE + ML).
Emily SRE: Handoff to next on-call @Darron Oncall in 30m; I'll stay for 5m overlap to confirm stability then update the ticket with timeline and graphs.
Marc PM: thanks everyone. Quick notes: customer comms drafted, no rollback needed (we shifted traffic), but rollout paused until ML confirms patch or safe config.
Jules Support: customer acknowledgements sent. No escalations at this time.
Priya ML: uploading memory profiles and kv logs to the ticket; initial hypothesis: v3.1 changed key eviction heuristics exposing a thrash pattern with long sequence workloads. Will propose quantization/eviction patch.
Emily SRE: closing thread but creating follow-up in #postmortems with links. Good job. :thumbsup:
